author: Lauren Branch
title: Crowd enjoy pickles, pigs and swigs at fifth annual festival in Mount Olive - NewsBreak
text:
By Lauren Branch ,
1 days ago
MOUNT OLIVE — After several back-to-back years of rain, the annual Pickles, Pigs and Swigs event was lucky to have perfect weather Nov. 7-8 in downtown Mount Olive.
The event was created in 2021 to promote downtown Mount Olive and to bring a fun event to town in the fall to compliment the springtime N.C. Pickle Festival, the only major festival in town. The event was hosted by the Mount Olive Area of Commerce and Mt. Olive Pickles.
Mt. Olive Pickles gave out pickle samples, the pickles for the event; the chamber gave out barbecue sandwiches, the pigs; and R&R Brewing sold beer, including the popular Pickletown Lager for the swigs, chamber President Julie Beck, the festival co-chair .
The weekend started with the barbecue cook-off that took place at 6 p.m. Nov. 7. Seventeen cook teams participated, and judging took place on the morning of Nov. 8. The top three winners won cash prizes and a chance to compete in the N.C. Pork Council Cook-Off.
This year’s winners were:
Dana Peterson with Showtime’s Legit BBQ, $1,200 prizeChris Fineran with Beach Boys BBQ, $600 prizeJason Baker with Baker Boys BBQ, $300 prize
Barbecue was sold on Nov. 8 during the festival for $12 a pound; sandwiches sold for $7 or two for $12.
“The highlight of the day for many was the barbecue sandwiches. Because we had more cook teams, we had more barbecue to sell. The remains will get sold by the pound until it is all gone,” Beck said.
During the festival Nov. 8, visitors could enjoy shopping with the vendors, pictures with Ollie the Pickle, a small car show, rides on the pickle train and more. The planning team added several activities this year they felt would make the festival better.
“We added two inflatables for children. We also had 13 vendors. We had a lot of photo opportunities, including a new PPS selfie spot; we had the pickle cut-outs and an inflatable pickle,” Beck said.
The festival was created as a fundraiser for the Downtown Development Corporation in an effort to establish and implement a strategic plan for downtown’s revitalization. The funds raised from the barbecue goes toward the cause in addition to sales of swag items such as T-shirts, hoodies, koozies and the newly added fleece-lined beanies. Items are still for sale at the Mount Olive Area Chamber of Commerce.
Live music was performed on the main stage in the Southern Bank lot on the corner of Main Street and Southeast Center Street.
“The fifth annual Pickles, Pigs and Swigs was successful. We had 17 cook teams, five more than we had in 2024, and the best weather ever! 582 South performed from 11-1, including a stunning rendition of the National Anthem. That was followed by Sack Lee and his band from 1:30-3 p.m. Melissa Kilpatrick and I ate the first barbecue sandwich of the day to kick off the event,” Beck said.
According to Beck, the sponsors and volunteers had a big impact on making the festival successful.
Smithfield’s Food was the presenting sponsor.
“Special shout-out to the UMO Baseball Team who volunteered all day and our sponsors: Mt. Olive Pickle, Southern Bank, R&R Brewery, Wayne County Travel and Tourism, Smithfield Foods, Prestige Farms and the Town of Mount Olive. Cheers to a ‘pig dill’ as we celebrated the fifth annual Pickles, Pigs, and Swigs Festival,” Beck said.
